doc.title: Doug Carn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2023

title: Jazz education and following the organists
summary: He gives a mixed view of jazz education and says he followed every organ player, from Jimmy Smith to Trudy Pitts.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Do you think that jazz education sort of the explosion of it in the last twenty years has been a good thing for the music?

Well in a way, see the music is very broad and there have been aspects to it you know. And one aspect that’s been making it accessible to musicians who ordinarily wouldn’t access it you know. And on the other hand it’s big in that kind of mundane and dry to people who loved it enough to run away from home and move to New York and sleep on the floor in an apartment in the Village and hang out until two or three in the morning and follow Kenny Garrett around, you know, and follow Mike Brecker around you know, follow you know —

Jimmy Smith. I followed all the organ players, every last one of them. Groove Holmes, Jimmy Smith, McDuff, Doctor Lonnie Smith, Shirley Scott. My uncle was good friends with Shirley and Stan and you know Trudy Pitts, Jimmy McGriff, I followed every one of them. You know I knew how they set up the organ, what kind of tunes they played using
the organ. You know some of them didn’t know what kind they was using themselves. But I followed all the organ players.
